summary: Reset canary images loader-diag-reset (Download word 0x12345601) and loader-diag-reset-bl (Bootloader word 0x1234560d, mode 3): the run-006 loader family (NAT-020 build-003 + NAT-022 --trig-hold --adt-aligned + NAT-026 payload fix) plus a six-hunk patch (entry PMU snapshot with clearing of a leftover Download/Bootloader request, a 45 s deadline measured from after the 83 s watchdog arm, RESET stage marker, RST report frames) and the unmodified NAT-042 reset module. Built twice with identical hashes, packaged into RECOVERY candidates (hashes only), 46 host/aarch64-simulator tests, 46/46 mutants killed, decision text for the native run (NAT-046) drafted and not dated. Nothing was flashed or run on the phone.
evidence_category: host-test (host x86 model + unicorn instruction-level simulation of the compiled loader); not a measurement of the S24

acceptance.1_build: build.py applies nat-022 patch_loader.py (--trig-hold --adt-aligned), nat-022 marker library, then patch_loader4.py (6 exact-match hunks, each anchor once, all-or-nothing); the NAT-042 module is linked unmodified (hashes equal to nat-042 sources: s5e9945_reset.h/.c); both images build with the loader flags and are reproducible (build-001 and build-002 image hashes identical).
acceptance.2_tests: test_nat044.py: 46 tests (system python: 31 run, 15 skipped for missing unicorn/capstone; interpreter with unicorn 2.1.4 + capstone: all 46 run). Layers: Patch (anchors, diff = hunks only), HostReset (real patched markerlib.c + markerlib4.c + NAT-042 module on x86 against a PMU register model), Build, Aarch64 (the built loader.elf in unicorn: trigger at the deadline after the RESET frame decoded from the framebuffer bytes, vendor register order and values, bootloader variant, read-back failure triggers nothing and is reported, unarmed never writes, leftover request cleared and reported, deadline armed only after the watchdog in the real recovery_guard). The deadline (45 s) is at most WDT (83 s) minus 20 s, enforced by build.py and tested. Mutation: 46 mutants of the new code, patch hunks, build rules and decoder; 46/46 killed, 0 invalid (mutation-002). The first run (mutation-001, 45 mutants) had two survivors and one invalid mutant, which exposed a tautological test and a missing ordering check; both fixed before mutation-002.

established: loader-diag-reset Image sha256 24baf94e039be4869361706356005bc19aa891a2ce170332f8a6ab2f718635a1; loader-diag-reset-bl Image sha256 87226d5246a906de28dfbfba2c479ca2698732c5103deca2b0f2654c899f8362; RECOVERY candidates e4cd7bdf4789b5bc60f8a0b3a0d5dd887ab75f345df13a0b0115a0934419fe4a and 7481c95ab8ef56a112507abb5cfa9e273285e32c7548264bb224ed5614832d2b.

In the instruction-level run of the compiled loader the PMU stores are INFORM2 byte 2 := 0x4e, INFORM3 := reason, reboot-cmd bits [2:0] := mode, 0x3c00 := 2, in that order, at the deadline (>= 45 s and < 45.05 s after the arm), after the RESET marker (0x41) was in the framebuffer; read-back failures (INFORM2, INFORM3, reboot-cmd) trigger nothing, are drawn as rc 2/3/4 and are not retried.

A leftover Download/Bootloader INFORM3 word is read before it is cleared, shown in the entry words, cleared with a read-back, and flagged CLEARED or CLEARFAIL in the status frame (decoded from the framebuffer).
start.S sets CPACR_EL1.FPEN and clears CPTR_EL2 before the first C call; the new code uses q/d register copies emitted by zig cc despite -mgeneral-regs-only, which is safe only inside the loader.
not_established: U1: that the loader's PMU stores reach the hardware; U2: that 0x3c00 := 2 resets without the ACPM STOP request; U3/U4: that S-Boot honours INFORM3 = Download / Bootloader. All are native measurements for NAT-046; unicorn and the host model have no caches, MMU or memory attributes and are not the S24.
That the reset marker is seen: it is on screen for milliseconds. That the phone returns to Download Mode, or to Android, by itself.
findings: The 'no SIMD in the text' check of my first version was vacuous (capstone disasm() stopped after two instructions) and its premise was wrong; replaced by the FPEN-before-C property and by a per-function ordering check (dsb sy between the INFORM3 clearing store and its read-back) in the compiled nat044_snapshot.
NAT-022's build.py already notes that zig cc emits SIMD with -mgeneral-regs-only; NAT-036's per-function SIMD test is sound.
